title: NYC pied-à-terre tax rollout must start again, judge rules
summary: The Staten Island judge voided the city’s 17,000 mailed notices to homeowners. The city is expected to challenge the decision, Politico reported.

title: Steep cuts to federal transit funding take effect Thursday
summary: Smaller communities and rural towns are "especially vulnerable” to the public transit and passenger rail cuts, according to the American Public Transportation Association.

title: Data centers are stress-testing local governments. Here are 5 strategies to rein them in.
summary: Tools including zoning and permitting can address transparency, infrastructure, community benefits and other concerns, panelists at a Southern Environmental Law Center event said.

title: With its first office-to-housing project done, Chicago advances ‘next chapter’ for its downtown
summary: The adaptive reuse project in the city's Loop has 117 mixed-income residential units. More conversions are in the pipeline.

title: State AGs push Congress for AI safety, transparency
summary: Their proposal would pause AI research until the creation of a federal department that would regulate the technology.

title: Amtrak Airo trains to start this week in Pacific Northwest
summary: The route serving Oregon, Washington and Vancouver, Canada, gets the first of Amtrak’s 83 new train sets.

title: Opportunity zones were meant to spur investment. Their impact is unclear, a GAO report shows.
summary: Revamped rules have reduced the number of low-income areas receiving the tax credits, the congressional watchdog found, and investment tends to flow to cities where development is already underway.

title: On clean energy, bigger is not always better
summary: When Congress revisits clean-energy tax policy, lawmakers should restore incentives for locally driven solar and storage projects, writes Edward Yim at Lawyers for Good Government.

title: Pittsburgh eyes quicker permitting with virtual inspections and a ‘fast lane’ for low-risk projects
summary: The first set of changes "will help applicants spend less time waiting and more time getting projects done," Mayor Corey O'Connor said.

title: Second federal judge overturns $7B Solar for All cancellation by Trump administration EPA
summary: The decision in a suit brought by Harris County, Texas, follows a similar ruling last week. A Harris County judge called it “a really important victory for energy resilience.”
